findings.blur: F1 score artificially improved under blur (up to 0.647). This is likely because Gaussian blur acts as a low-pass filter, attenuating high-frequency noise and standardizing the spectral signatures for the 146 specific test images, removing variance that previously confused the model.
findings.resize: Similar to blur, downscaling involves anti-aliasing filters which modify high frequencies. The apparent 'improvement' is an artifact of the specific test set losing confusing details, not true cross-generator robustness.

conclusion: The SVM model relies on delicate high-frequency artifacts. While it showed some resilience, perturbations that actively destroy high frequencies fundamentally alter the image spectrum. The higher scores do not imply the model is 'more robust' when blurred; rather, the test set simply became easier to classify due to reduced variance.
